stem: Charu lists these living things from a farm visit: banyan, peacock, goat, spinach, and lizard.

parts.text: Which grouping uses a valid observable basis?

options.text: Banyan and spinach together as plants; peacock, goat, and lizard together as animals.
Banyan with goat because both are said to bring good luck.
Peacock with lizard only because animals can be grouped only by where they live.
Goat with peacock because both names start with a hard consonant sound.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Grouping by plant versus animal uses observable features shared within each group.

teacher.key_rationale: A valid basis uses observable similarities and differences such as plant versus animal. Luck, living-place-only rules, and name sounds are not valid observable grouping bases here.
